This iconic photograph, known as 'Migrant Mother,' was taken by Dorothea Lange in 1936 in Nipomo, California. It shows Florence Owens Thompson, a 32-year-old mother of seven, with a deeply worried expression, her hand touching her face. Two of her children lean against her shoulders with their faces turned away from the camera. The photograph was taken to document conditions facing migrant farmworkers during the Great Depression.

(Photograph by Dorothea Lange, 1936. Library of Congress, Farm Security Administration/Office of War Information Collection.)

The FSA photography project produced some of the most enduring images of the Depression era. Choice A refers to a different New Deal agency focused on employment. Choice C is a wartime propaganda agency. Choice D is a relief organization, not a government photography program.

items.stem: A geographer studying the Great Plains in the 1930s finds that the most severe Dust Bowl damage occurred in areas that had been converted from native grassland to wheat farms after 1900. Which conclusion about the Dust Bowl's causes is BEST supported by this evidence?
items.stemEs: Un geógrafo que estudia las Grandes Llanuras en la década de 1930 encuentra que el daño más severo del Dust Bowl ocurrió en áreas que habían sido convertidas de praderas nativas a granjas de trigo después de 1900. ¿Qué conclusión sobre las causas del Dust Bowl está MEJOR respaldada por esta evidencia?

choices.text: The Dust Bowl was caused entirely by a prolonged drought cycle that was made worse by the unusually high temperatures of the 1930s across the Great Plains.
choices.textEs: El Dust Bowl fue causado por un ciclo de sequía prolongado que empeoró por las temperaturas inusualmente altas de la década de 1930 en las Grandes Llanuras.

choices.text: Overgrazing by cattle on the Great Plains removed the grass cover, allowing drought conditions to turn the exposed soil into dust.
choices.textEs: El sobrepastoreo del ganado en las Grandes Llanuras eliminó la cubierta de hierba, lo que permitió que las condiciones de sequía convirtieran el suelo expuesto en polvo.

choices.text: Agricultural practices that replaced deep-rooted native grasses with shallow-rooted crops left the soil without the anchor needed to withstand drought conditions, making human land use a critical cause of the crisis.
choices.textEs: Las prácticas agrícolas que reemplazaron los pastos nativos de raíces profundas con cultivos de raíces poco profundas dejaron el suelo sin el ancla necesaria para resistir las condiciones de sequía, convirtiendo el uso humano de la tierra en una causa crítica de la crisis.

choices.text: The Federal government's policy of encouraging wheat production through price supports drove farmers to convert fragile lands to cultivation, making government policy the root cause of the Dust Bowl.
choices.textEs: La política del gobierno federal de fomentar la producción de trigo mediante subsidios de precios llevó a los agricultores a convertir tierras frágiles al cultivo, convirtiendo la política gubernamental en la causa raíz del Dust Bowl.

items.explanation: The conversion of native grassland to wheat farms eliminated deep-rooted grasses whose root systems held the soil in place. When drought struck and crops failed, there were no native root systems to anchor the topsoil, making it vulnerable to wind erosion on a catastrophic scale. This evidence directly implicates human agricultural practices — not drought alone — as a cause of the Dust Bowl. The geographer's finding requires students to reason from geographic evidence to a causal conclusion about the interaction of human and natural factors.
items.explanationEs: La conversión de praderas nativas a granjas de trigo eliminó los pastos de raíces profundas cuyos sistemas radiculares mantenían el suelo en su lugar. Cuando la sequía azotó y las cosechas fallaron, no había sistemas de raíces nativas para anclar la capa superior del suelo, haciéndolo vulnerable a la erosión eólica a escala catastrófica. Esta evidencia implica directamente las prácticas agrícolas humanas — no solo la sequía — como causa del Dust Bowl.

choices.text: Because California had strong labor unions, Dust Bowl migrants were quickly absorbed into the workforce at fair wages, but they faced intense social discrimination from urban Californians.

items.explanation: The Dust Bowl migration created a surplus labor supply that depressed wages in California agriculture, benefiting growers while harming both migrant and existing local workers. At the same time, the migrants faced discrimination and social hostility, creating new social tensions. This analysis integrates geographic displacement, economic impact (wage depression), and social impact (discrimination, community conflict) — the full range of consequences the standard requires students to analyze. Students must synthesize multiple dimensions of impact rather than recall one fact.
items.explanationEs: La migración del Dust Bowl creó una oferta excedente de mano de obra que deprimió los salarios en la agricultura de California, beneficiando a los agricultores mientras perjudicaba tanto a los trabajadores migrantes como a los trabajadores locales existentes. Al mismo tiempo, los migrantes enfrentaron discriminación y hostilidad social, creando nuevas tensiones sociales. Este análisis integra el desplazamiento geográfico, el impacto económico (depresión salarial) y el impacto social (discriminación, conflicto comunitario).

items.stem: A student compares two maps: one showing the distribution of native short-grass prairie on the Great Plains in 1870, and a second showing the areas of greatest soil erosion during the 1930s Dust Bowl. The maps show nearly identical geographic footprints. Which conclusion is BEST supported by comparing these two maps?
items.stemEs: Un estudiante compara dos mapas: uno que muestra la distribución de la pradera nativa de pasto corto en las Grandes Llanuras en 1870, y un segundo que muestra las áreas de mayor erosión del suelo durante el Dust Bowl de la década de 1930. Los mapas muestran contornos geográficos casi idénticos. ¿Qué conclusión está MEJOR respaldada al comparar estos dos mapas?

choices.text: Drought conditions were worst in areas that had historically supported native short-grass prairie, suggesting that these specific regions had uniquely severe and persistent long-term climate cycles that made farming them inherently and unavoidably risky.
choices.textEs: Las condiciones de sequía fueron peores en las áreas que históricamente habían albergado praderas nativas de pasto corto, lo que sugiere que los patrones climáticos en esas regiones eran únicamente severos.

choices.text: Native short-grass prairie lands attracted substantially denser farm settlement than other Great Plains regions, which concentrated the effects of poor agricultural practices and magnified the scale of topsoil loss in those particular areas.
choices.textEs: Las tierras de pradera nativa de pasto corto estaban más densamente pobladas por agricultores, lo que aumentó la escala de las malas prácticas agrícolas en esas áreas específicas.

choices.text: Short-grass prairies had historically extremely thin topsoil layers that made them permanently and fundamentally unsuitable for sustained agricultural use even before widespread Euro-American settlement of the Great Plains region.
choices.textEs: Las praderas de pasto corto tenían históricamente una delgada capa de suelo que las hacía permanentemente inadecuadas para la agricultura incluso antes del asentamiento humano de las Grandes Llanuras.

choices.text: Converting fragile native grasslands to cropland removed the natural soil-anchoring system; when drought struck, those converted lands suffered the worst erosion — making human agricultural expansion the key causal factor.
choices.textEs: La conversión de pastizales nativos ecológicamente frágiles en tierras de cultivo eliminó el sistema natural de anclaje del suelo, y cuando llegó la sequía, esas tierras convertidas sufrieron la peor erosión, lo que convierte la expansión agrícola humana en el factor causal clave.

items.explanation: If the areas of greatest Dust Bowl damage correspond precisely to the areas that had been native short-grass prairie, it strongly implies that those lands were ecologically unsuited for crop agriculture — the native grasses had evolved to hold soil in drought conditions, and replacing them with crops removed that protection. The overlap between formerly-prairie land and damaged land is strong evidence that the agricultural conversion of fragile grassland ecosystems was a primary cause of the ecological disaster. This requires geographic reasoning and evidence evaluation — DOK 3.
items.explanationEs: Si las áreas de mayor daño del Dust Bowl corresponden precisamente a las áreas que habían sido praderas nativas de pasto corto, esto implica fuertemente que esas tierras eran ecológicamente inadecuadas para la agricultura de cultivos. Los pastos nativos habían evolucionado para retener el suelo en condiciones de sequía, y su reemplazo por cultivos eliminó esa protección. La superposición entre la tierra anteriormente de pradera y la tierra dañada es evidencia sólida de que la conversión agrícola de frágiles ecosistemas de pastizales fue una causa principal del desastre ecológico.

items.stem: The Dust Bowl caused geographic, social, and economic disruption simultaneously. A student is asked to rank these three types of impact by their long-term significance. Which argument provides the STRONGEST justification for ranking the economic impact as most significant in the long term?
items.stemEs: El Dust Bowl causó disrupciones geográficas, sociales y económicas simultáneamente. A un estudiante se le pide que clasifique estos tres tipos de impacto según su importancia a largo plazo. ¿Qué argumento proporciona la justificación MÁS SÓLIDA para clasificar el impacto económico como el más significativo a largo plazo?

choices.text: The economic impact was most significant because the loss of farm income forced millions of Americans into poverty, and poverty was the defining experience of the Great Depression era.
choices.textEs: El impacto económico fue el más significativo porque la pérdida de ingresos agrícolas sumió a millones de estadounidenses en la pobreza, y la pobreza fue la experiencia definitoria de la era de la Gran Depresión.

choices.text: The economic impact was most significant because the collapse of Great Plains agriculture permanently restructured American farming, drove lasting demographic shifts through mass migration, and compelled federal intervention that altered agricultural policy for generations.
choices.textEs: El impacto económico fue el más significativo porque el colapso de la agricultura de las Grandes Llanuras reestructuró permanentemente la agricultura estadounidense, impulsó cambios demográficos duraderos a través de la migración masiva y obligó a una intervención federal que alteró la política agrícola durante generaciones.

choices.text: The geographic impact was most significant because topsoil loss permanently reduced the agricultural productivity of the Great Plains, and no policy or social change could restore what the wind had carried away.
choices.textEs: El impacto geográfico fue el más significativo porque la pérdida de la capa superficial del suelo redujo permanentemente la productividad agrícola de las Grandes Llanuras, y ninguna política o cambio social podía restaurar lo que el viento se había llevado.

choices.text: The social impact was most significant because the migration of Okies to California created lasting ethnic and class tensions that shaped California politics and labor relations through the rest of the twentieth century.
choices.textEs: El impacto social fue el más significativo porque la migración de los 'Okies' a California creó tensiones étnicas y de clase duraderas que moldearon la política de California y las relaciones laborales durante el resto del siglo XX.

items.explanation: The economic impact was most significant long-term because the destruction of Great Plains agriculture drove mass migration that permanently depopulated entire counties, eliminated the small-farm economy of the region, and forced federal intervention through New Deal agricultural programs that permanently restructured the relationship between the federal government and American farming. The geographic damage (erosion) was partially reversible; the social disruption (migration) had lasting demographic effects; but the economic restructuring of American agriculture was permanent. Students must evaluate competing arguments and justify a conclusion — a hallmark of DOK 3.
items.explanationEs: El impacto económico fue el más significativo a largo plazo porque la destrucción de la agricultura de las Grandes Llanuras impulsó una migración masiva que despobló permanentemente condados enteros, eliminó la economía de pequeñas granjas de la región y forzó la intervención federal a través de programas agrícolas del New Deal que reestructuraron permanentemente la relación entre el gobierno federal y la agricultura estadounidense.

items.stem: This photograph was created as part of a federal program designed to:

choices.text: Promote tourism to California's agricultural regions
Document rural poverty and build support for New Deal relief programs
Encourage migration from the Midwest to the West Coast
Recruit workers for wartime aircraft factories

items.explanation: The photograph was made for the federal photography project run under the Resettlement Administration and then the Farm Security Administration, whose purpose was to document rural hardship and build public support for New Deal relief. Choice A is wrong because the images showed poverty rather than promoting tourism. Choice D is wrong because wartime recruitment came later, after 1941. Dorothea Lange's and Walker Evans's work from this project became the visual record of the Depression.

items.stem: Which conclusion about the Marshall Plan is best supported by the fact that it offered economic reconstruction aid to all European nations, including those within the Soviet sphere of influence?

choices.text: American policymakers genuinely expected the Soviet Union to participate in the Marshall Plan and integrate its economy into Western trade networks.
The Marshall Plan was designed primarily as a humanitarian relief program to prevent civilian starvation in postwar Europe.
American policymakers believed that economic recovery would reduce the appeal of communist political movements in war-devastated European nations.
The offer to Soviet-aligned nations demonstrated that the United States did not yet view the Soviet Union as a long-term strategic adversary.

items.explanation: Secretary of State Marshall and the State Department's planning explicitly identified economic desperation as the primary recruiter for communist parties in Western Europe. Rebuilding prosperity was a strategic counter to Soviet political influence, not merely humanitarian charity.

items.stem:
Extended Response — No sources are provided for this question. Draw entirely on your knowledge of U.S. history.

The Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA), created in 1933, was frequently called the most radical experiment of the New Deal. Unlike most other New Deal agencies, the TVA involved the federal government directly owning and operating infrastructure — dams, power plants, and transmission lines — across a seven-state region centered on the Tennessee River.

Write an extended response that constructs and defends an argument in answer to the following question:

Was the Tennessee Valley Authority a model of successful federal regional development, and what does the TVA's impact on Tennessee reveal about the broader possibilities and limits of New Deal-era government intervention?

Your response MUST:
1. State a clear, specific, and defensible claim about the TVA's success as a model of federal regional development.
2. Support your argument with at least THREE specific pieces of historical evidence about the TVA's impact on Tennessee and/or the Tennessee Valley region (economic, social, environmental, or political).
3. Acknowledge and address at least ONE significant limitation, criticism, or unintended consequence of the TVA's approach.
4. Connect the TVA model to the broader question of when and how federal intervention in regional economic development is most effective — drawing at least ONE comparison to another federal development initiative from a different era of U.S. history (before or after the New Deal).

Use the CER (Claim-Evidence-Reasoning) framework throughout.
items.stemEs:
Respuesta Extendida — No se proporcionan fuentes para esta pregunta. Basa tu respuesta completamente en tu conocimiento de la historia de los EE.UU.

La Autoridad del Valle de Tennessee (TVA), creada en 1933, fue frecuentemente llamada el experimento más radical del New Deal. A diferencia de la mayoría de las otras agencias del New Deal, la TVA involucró al gobierno federal en la propiedad directa y operación de infraestructura — represas, plantas de energía y líneas de transmisión — en una región de siete estados centrada en el río Tennessee.

Escriba una respuesta extendida que construya y defienda un argumento en respuesta a la siguiente pregunta:

¿Fue la Autoridad del Valle de Tennessee un modelo de desarrollo regional federal exitoso, y qué revela el impacto de la TVA en Tennessee sobre las posibilidades más amplias y los límites de la intervención gubernamental de la era del New Deal?

Su respuesta DEBE:
1. Enunciar una afirmación clara, específica y defendible sobre el éxito de la TVA como modelo de desarrollo regional federal.
2. Apoyar su argumento con al menos TRES piezas específicas de evidencia histórica sobre el impacto de la TVA en Tennessee y/o la región del Valle de Tennessee (económico, social, ambiental o político).
3. Reconocer y abordar al menos UNA limitación significativa, crítica o consecuencia no intencionada del enfoque de la TVA.
4. Conectar el modelo de la TVA con la pregunta más amplia de cuándo y cómo la intervención federal en el desarrollo económico regional es más efectiva — haciendo al menos UNA comparación con otra iniciativa de desarrollo federal de una era diferente de la historia de los EE.UU. (antes o después del New Deal).

Use el marco CER (Afirmación-Evidencia-Razonamiento) a lo largo de su respuesta.
items.correctAnswer: A top-score (4-point) extended response will: (1) CLAIM: A defensible specific claim — e.g., 'The TVA was a qualified but meaningful success: it achieved transformative electrification and flood control in a severely underdeveloped region, but its displacement of rural communities and racially segregated employment practices reveal that New Deal federal intervention could simultaneously modernize and marginalize.' (2) EVIDENCE (minimum three Tennessee/TVA-specific): Norris Dam (completed 1936, Anderson/Campbell counties, Tennessee — first TVA dam, controlled Tennessee River flooding); rural electrification — by 1940, the TVA had extended electricity to approximately 90% of the Tennessee Valley, transforming farm productivity and quality of life where private utilities had refused to invest; dramatic reduction in electricity rates (TVA's average residential rate was among the lowest in the nation by 1940, compared to private utilities); flood control eliminated the chronic Tennessee River flooding that had repeatedly destroyed agricultural land and infrastructure; Muscle Shoals fertilizer production provided affordable nitrate fertilizers to Valley farmers; the creation of Norris, Tennessee — a planned TVA company town — as a model of social planning. (3) Limitations and criticisms: The TVA displaced approximately 15,000 families from reservoir areas (many poor, rural Tennessee families who received inadequate compensation); TVA employment was racially segregated throughout the 1930s and 1940s, with Black workers excluded from TVA planned towns like Norris; private utility opposition was intense (Wendell Willkie / Commonwealth and Southern) and the model was never replicated nationally; the TVA was challenged in Ashwander v. TVA (1936) but upheld. (4) Cross-era comparison: Federal regional development comparisons include: the Homestead Act (1862) as federal land distribution to encourage Western settlement — similar in scale but relied on individual enterprise rather than federal ownership; the Interstate Highway System (1956, Eisenhower) as federal infrastructure investment without federal ownership; or the Marshall Plan (1948) as federal development investment abroad. Strong responses might compare TVA to Great Society-era Appalachian Regional Commission (1965), which continued federal development investment in Tennessee and Appalachia. CER explicit throughout.
items.dokRationale: Student must synthesize the TVA's design (US.42), the broader New Deal philosophy (US.41), and the regional development context of the Depression (US.40) without source scaffolding, connecting the TVA to a broader U.S. history pattern of federal regional development — requiring the highest level of independent cross-era historical reasoning with Tennessee specificity.
items.explanation:
SCORING GUIDE (4 points):
4 - Exemplary: States a precise, specific claim about the TVA's qualified success that acknowledges both achievements and limitations. Presents three or more specific, accurate pieces of Tennessee/TVA historical evidence with concrete detail (names of dams, electrification rates, displacement figures, etc.). Addresses at least one significant limitation with accuracy and fairness. Makes a substantive cross-era comparison with historically accurate content. CER framework fully applied. Writing demonstrates deep, nuanced understanding of the TVA's historical significance.
3 - Proficient: States a defensible claim. Presents three pieces of TVA/Tennessee evidence with reasonable accuracy. Addresses one limitation. Provides a cross-era comparison with basic accuracy. CER applied but reasoning may be underdeveloped.
2 - Developing: States a general claim about the TVA. Presents two pieces of evidence, one of which may be vague. Acknowledges limitations in a general way. Cross-era comparison absent or superficial. CER partially applied.
1 - Beginning: Makes a general statement about the TVA without a specific claim. Evidence is generic (e.g., 'the TVA built dams and provided electricity'). No limitation addressed. No cross-era comparison. No CER structure.
0 - No response or completely off-topic.

KEY EVIDENCE EXPECTED: Norris Dam (1936, Anderson/Campbell counties, TN); rural electrification rates by 1940 (~90% of Tennessee Valley); reduction in TVA electricity rates vs. private utilities; flood control on the Tennessee River; Muscle Shoals fertilizer/nitrate production; displacement of ~15,000 families from reservoir areas; racial segregation in TVA employment and town planning (Norris, TN); Ashwander v. TVA (1936); Wendell Willkie / Commonwealth and Southern opposition; Appalachian Regional Commission (1965) as cross-era comparison.

SYNTHESIS EXPECTATIONS: Response should connect the TVA's specific Tennessee impacts to the broader question of when federal regional development is effective, drawing a comparison to another era's approach. Strong responses will note the TVA's irreplication — no other regional authority of its scope was created — as itself significant evidence about the limits of the model.
items.explanationEs:
GUÍA DE PUNTUACIÓN (4 puntos):
4 - Ejemplar: Enuncia una afirmación precisa y específica sobre el éxito calificado de la TVA que reconoce tanto logros como limitaciones. Presenta tres o más piezas específicas y precisas de evidencia histórica de Tennessee/TVA con detalles concretos (nombres de represas, tasas de electrificación, cifras de desplazamiento, etc.). Aborda al menos una limitación significativa con precisión y equidad. Hace una comparación inter-época sustantiva con contenido históricamente preciso. El marco CER está completamente aplicado. La escritura demuestra una comprensión profunda y matizada del significado histórico de la TVA.
3 - Competente: Enuncia una afirmación defendible. Presenta tres piezas de evidencia de la TVA/Tennessee con razonable precisión. Aborda una limitación. Proporciona una comparación inter-época con precisión básica. CER aplicado pero el razonamiento puede estar poco desarrollado.
2 - En desarrollo: Enuncia una afirmación general sobre la TVA. Presenta dos piezas de evidencia, una de las cuales puede ser vaga. Reconoce las limitaciones de manera general. Comparación inter-época ausente o superficial. CER parcialmente aplicado.
1 - Inicial: Hace una declaración general sobre la TVA sin una afirmación específica. La evidencia es genérica (p. ej., 'la TVA construyó represas y proporcionó electricidad'). Sin limitación abordada. Sin comparación inter-época. Sin estructura CER.
0 - Sin respuesta o completamente fuera del tema.

EVIDENCIA CLAVE ESPERADA: Presa Norris (1936, condados de Anderson y Campbell, TN); tasas de electrificación rural para 1940 (~90% del Valle de Tennessee); reducción de las tarifas de electricidad de la TVA vs. servicios públicos privados; control de inundaciones en el río Tennessee; producción de fertilizantes/nitratos de Muscle Shoals; desplazamiento de ~15,000 familias de áreas de embalse; segregación racial en el empleo y planificación urbana de la TVA (Norris, TN); Ashwander v. TVA (1936); oposición de Wendell Willkie / Commonwealth and Southern; Comisión Regional Apalache (1965) como comparación inter-época.

EXPECTATIVAS DE SÍNTESIS: La respuesta debe conectar los impactos específicos de la TVA en Tennessee con la pregunta más amplia de cuándo el desarrollo regional federal es efectivo, haciendo una comparación con el enfoque de otra era. Las respuestas sólidas señalarán la no replicación de la TVA — ninguna otra autoridad regional de su alcance fue creada — como evidencia significativa sobre los límites del modelo.
